faqs.a:
(a)
The authority has the right to acquire by eminent domain any property, real or personal,
               which it may deem necessary to carry out the purposes of this article after the adoption
               by it of a resolution declaring that the acquisition of the property described therein
               is in the public interest and necessary for public use. The authority may exercise
               the power of eminent domain pursuant to the provisions of either C.R.S. §§ 38-1-101
               to 38-1-115, C.R.S. §§ 38-3-101 et seq., 38-5-106 or C.R.S. § 38-6-101 et seq.
(b)
Property already devoted to a public use may be acquired; but no property belonging
               to the city or to any government may be acquired without its consent, and no property
               belonging to a public utility corporation may be acquired without the approval of
               the commission or other officer or tribunal having regulatory power over such corporation.
(Code 1981, § 14-23; Ord. No. 1248, § 9, 6-16-1975)
State Law reference—
Similar provisions, C.R.S. § 29-4-211.
